content: Give Claude Code the same rule visibility and edit-time enforcement as other agents, strictly repository-local: no global configuration, no CLI modification, inert for non-Claude tools.

CLAUDE.md is a one-line @AGENTS.md import rather than a copy: Claude Code natively expands @-imports, so the two entry files cannot drift into conflicting rulebooks. The validator now requires that import line whenever CLAUDE.md exists and rejects a malformed .claude/settings.json; both rules are inert when the bridge is absent.

The .claude/hooks/pre_edit.py PreToolUse guard blocks, at edit time and before anything lands: rewrites of agent/progress/checkpoints/ (immutable history) and any edit outside agent/ while no session is in progress. Each denial carries its remediation command. The guard fails open on schema drift by design; the pre-commit gate and Nix checks remain the hard, tool-agnostic gates.

Scope guarantees recorded in .claude/README.md and AGENTS.md: nothing writes to ~/.claude, nothing modifies the CLI, the bridge is inert for non-Claude tools, and Claude Code itself asks each user to approve project-level hooks before they run.

Test the guard paths live with stdin JSON payloads before committing: checkpoint edit, non-agent edit without a session, agent/ edit, malformed stdin, session_start banner, then non-agent edit after scaffolding.

All six paths behaved as designed: checkpoint edit denied (exit 2), non-agent edit denied without a session (exit 2 with the scaffold command), agent/ edit allowed, malformed stdin failed open (exit 0), banner printed, and the same non-agent edit was allowed after scaffolding this session. One denial message was reworded for clarity before committing.

Validator self-test extended to 23 cases (valid bridge, CLAUDE.md duplicating rules instead of importing, broken settings JSON). Final verification: self-test 23/23, repository records ok (8 sessions, 63 events, 77 Markdown), dev preset 16/16, pre-commit hook ran on the implementation commit.
